claims.head: The schedule did the Sharks no favors
claims.body: It’s the Sharks’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Canadiens get more of the play than usual.

claims.head: The Canadiens hunt better looks than the Sharks
claims.body: The Canadiens wait for good looks, but the Sharks settle for hopeful ones. Montréal is near the top of the league for shot quality, and San Jose is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should be the Canadiens’.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 33% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

MTL.head: Advantage, the Canadiens
MTL.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while San Jose is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Sharks’ way back in is getting good looks.

SJS.head: The Sharks face a real test
SJS.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while San Jose is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Sharks can pull it off if they get good looks.
